claim: By default, EventBridge retries sending an event to a target for 24 hours and up to 185 times, with exponential back off and jitter; the retry policy settings of the target set the length of time and the number of retry attempts.
question: EventBridge retry policy for a target: default maximum event age and maximum retry attempts; what is configurable?

qualifiers.scope: per target of a rule (retry policy setting)
qualifiers.condition: Retriable errors only; configured in the Retry policy settings of the target.

evidence.quote: You set the length of time it tries, and number of retry attempts in the Retry policy settings for the target. By default, EventBridge retries sending the event for 24 hours and up to 185 times with an exponential back off and jitter, or randomized delay.

claim: If an event is not delivered after all retry attempts are exhausted, the event is dropped and EventBridge does not continue to process it; a dead-letter queue can receive failed events.
question: What happens to an EventBridge event after all retries to a target fail?

values.display: configure a dead-letter queue (DLQ) to receive all failed events

evidence.quote: If an event isn't delivered after all retry attempts are exhausted, the event is dropped and EventBridge doesn't continue to process it. To avoid losing events after they fail to be delivered to a target, configure a dead-letter queue (DLQ) to receive all failed events.

claim: When you create an EventBridge archive you can specify the number of days to retain events; by default, EventBridge stores events in an archive indefinitely.
question: EventBridge archive retention options (number of days or indefinite)?

values.display: stores events in an archive indefinitely
the number of days to retain events in the archive

evidence.quote: You can specify the number of days to retain events in the archive. By default, EventBridge stores events in an archive indefinitely.

claim: Each EventBridge archive receives events from a single source event bus, and the source event bus cannot be changed once the archive is created; several archives can exist for one bus.
question: Can an EventBridge archive take events from more than one bus, or change its source bus?

values.display: You cannot change the source event bus once an archive is created

evidence.quote: Each archive receives events from a single source event bus. You cannot change the source event bus once an archive is created. You can create multiple archives for a given event bus.

claim: With PutEvents on Custom Event Bus - Classic, you can batch up to 10 event entries into one request.
question: EventBridge PutEvents entries per request?

qualifiers.condition: Classic PutEvents page; the new Custom Event Bus allows up to 100 entries and is not examinable yet.

evidence.quote: When you send custom events to EventBridge using the PutEvents action, you can batch up to 10 event entries into one request for efficiency.

note: The new Custom Event Bus (GA 2026-09-24) allows 1 to 100 entries per PutEvents request: not examinable yet.

claim: The total PutEvents request size, which is the sum of all event entries in the request, must be less than 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes); the limit applies to the request as a whole, and a single event can use up to the full 1 MB if it is the only entry.
question: EventBridge maximum event size (PutEvents entry), and how the size is calculated?

qualifiers.scope: per PutEvents request, all entries together

evidence.quote: The total request size—that is, the sum of all event entries in the request—must be less than 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes). This limit applies to the request as a whole, not to individual entries. A single event can use up to the full 1 MB if it is the only entry in the request.

note: Older material and exam questions assume a 256 KB event size; the 1 MB limit is dated 2026-01 in What's New (the decisions+changes lens records the change).

claim: EventBridge calculates a PutEvents entry size from the Time parameter (14 bytes, if specified), the UTF-8 byte length of Source and DetailType, and, if specified, the UTF-8 byte length of Detail and of each Resources entry.
question: How does EventBridge calculate the size of a PutEvents entry?

values.display: the number of bytes for their UTF-8 encoded forms

evidence.quote: EventBridge calculates the PutEventsRequestEntry size as follows: If specified, the Time parameter is 14 bytes. The Source and DetailType parameters are the number of bytes for their UTF-8 encoded forms. If specified, the Detail parameter is the number of bytes for its UTF-8 encoded form. If specified, each entry of the Resources parameter is the number of bytes for its UTF-8 encoded forms.

claim: If a PutEvents entry is larger than 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes), AWS recommends uploading the event to an Amazon S3 bucket and including the Object URL in the PutEvents entry.
question: What does AWS recommend for an EventBridge event larger than the entry size limit?

values.display: uploading the event to an Amazon S3 bucket

evidence.quote: If the entry size is larger than 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes), we recommend uploading the event to an Amazon S3 bucket and including the Object URL in the PutEvents entry.

claim: In an EventBridge Scheduler retry policy, MaximumEventAgeInSeconds, the maximum time to continue to make retry attempts, can be set from 60 to 86400 seconds.
question: EventBridge Scheduler retry policy maximums: maximum event age?

qualifiers.scope: per schedule target retry policy; seconds

evidence.quote: The maximum amount of time, in seconds, to continue to make retry attempts. Type: Integer Valid Range: Minimum value of 60. Maximum value of 86400.

claim: In an EventBridge Scheduler retry policy, MaximumRetryAttempts can be set from 0 to 185; retries with exponential backoff continue until the maximum attempts are made or the MaximumEventAgeInSeconds is reached.
question: EventBridge Scheduler retry policy maximums: maximum retry attempts?

evidence.quote: The maximum number of retry attempts to make before the request fails. Retry attempts with exponential backoff continue until either the maximum number of attempts is made or until the duration of the MaximumEventAgeInSeconds is reached. Type: Integer Valid Range: Minimum value of 0. Maximum value of 185.

claim: The EventBridge Scheduler flexible time window MaximumWindowInMinutes, the maximum time window during which a schedule can be invoked, can be set from 1 to 1440 minutes.
question: EventBridge Scheduler flexible time window maximum?

evidence.quote: The maximum time window during which a schedule can be invoked. Type: Integer Valid Range: Minimum value of 1. Maximum value of 1440.

note: The value is in minutes (the parameter name MaximumWindowInMinutes); the page quote does not repeat the unit.

claim: The maximum size of an EventBridge Scheduler target's Input payload is 256 KB; this is a fixed limit, not an adjustable Service Quotas quota.
question: EventBridge Scheduler: maximum target Input payload size?

qualifiers.condition: Applies to all target types, templated and universal.

evidence.quote: The maximum size of a target's Input payload is 256 KB. This limit applies to the Input field on a schedule's target for all target types.
The Input API parameter has a fixed limit, not an adjustable Service Quotas quota.
